levels.title: Fix a typo with REPLACE
levels.task: Stellar Sound’s training slice is song ids 1001 through 1005. The roster has a misspelled artist: use REPLACE on artist so every 'Lipppa' becomes 'Lipa'. Show two columns: track_name, then REPLACE(...) AS artist_clean (use that exact alias). Sort by track_name alphabetically.
levels.solution:
SELECT track_name,
  REPLACE(artist, 'Lipppa', 'Lipa') AS artist_clean
FROM top_songs
WHERE id BETWEEN 1001 AND 1005
ORDER BY track_name;
levels.hintMessage: REPLACE(artist, 'Lipppa', 'Lipa') AS artist_clean. WHERE id BETWEEN 1001 AND 1005. ORDER BY track_name.
levels.successMessage: Nice! REPLACE swaps only the matching substring—everyone else stays untouched.

levels.title: Normalize a label with REPLACE
levels.task: Marketing wants the word 'Hip Hop' without a hyphen in slides. From top_songs, return only rows where genre is exactly 'Hip-Hop'. Show track_name and REPLACE(genre, 'Hip-Hop', 'Hip Hop') AS genre_display (copy the alias). Sort by track_name alphabetically.
levels.initialCode: -- WHERE genre = 'Hip-Hop' ... REPLACE(genre, 'Hip-Hop', 'Hip Hop') AS genre_display
levels.solution:
SELECT track_name,
  REPLACE(genre, 'Hip-Hop', 'Hip Hop') AS genre_display
FROM top_songs
WHERE genre = 'Hip-Hop'
ORDER BY track_name;
levels.hintMessage: Filter with WHERE genre = 'Hip-Hop'. Second column: REPLACE(genre, 'Hip-Hop', 'Hip Hop') AS genre_display (space, no hyphen). ORDER BY track_name.
levels.successMessage: Good! Same data, friendlier label—no need to edit the table.

levels.title: Friendly labels with CASE
levels.task: Still at Stellar Sound, ids 1001–1005: show track_name and a column label. If the label is missing after a LEFT JOIN to album_info on album_name, show exactly the text 'No label info' (copy spelling). If it exists, show the real label. Use CASE ... END AS label. Sort by track_name.
levels.initialCode: -- CASE WHEN a.label IS NULL THEN 'No label info' ELSE a.label END AS label
levels.solution:
SELECT t.track_name,
  CASE WHEN a.label IS NULL THEN 'No label info' ELSE a.label END AS label
FROM top_songs t
LEFT JOIN album_info a ON t.album_name = a.album_name
WHERE t.id BETWEEN 1001 AND 1005
ORDER BY t.track_name;
levels.hintMessage: LEFT JOIN album_info ON album_name. CASE WHEN a.label IS NULL THEN 'No label info' ELSE a.label END AS label. ORDER BY t.track_name.
levels.successMessage: Perfect! CASE turns NULLs into human-readable text for the same report.

levels.title: Bucket rows with CASE
levels.task: For chart songs with ids 1 through 5 only, return id, track_name, and one column chart_segment built with CASE on weeks_on_chart: if weeks_on_chart is 40 or more, use exactly 'Long run'; if 20 or more (but under 40), use exactly 'Solid weeks'; otherwise use exactly 'Fresh entry'. Sort by id ascending.
levels.initialCode: -- CASE WHEN weeks_on_chart >= 40 THEN 'Long run' WHEN ... END AS chart_segment
levels.solution:
SELECT id,
  track_name,
  CASE
    WHEN weeks_on_chart >= 40 THEN 'Long run'
    WHEN weeks_on_chart >= 20 THEN 'Solid weeks'
    ELSE 'Fresh entry'
  END AS chart_segment
FROM top_songs
WHERE id BETWEEN 1 AND 5
ORDER BY id;
levels.hintMessage: Three branches: >=40, then >=20, then ELSE. Spelling must match: 'Long run', 'Solid weeks', 'Fresh entry'. ORDER BY id.
levels.successMessage: Great! CASE is ideal for turning one numeric column into simple story buckets.

levels.title: REPLACE and CASE together
levels.task: Training ids 1001–1005 again. Build three columns: track_name; artist_fixed as REPLACE(artist, 'Lipppa', 'Lipa') (use that exact alias); and stream_story from CASE on spotify_streams—if 2 billion or more, exactly 'Mega hit'; if 1 billion or more (but under 2 billion), exactly 'Big streams'; otherwise exactly 'Growing'. Sort by track_name alphabetically.
levels.initialCode: -- REPLACE(...) AS artist_fixed, CASE WHEN spotify_streams >= ... END AS stream_story
levels.solution:
SELECT track_name,
  REPLACE(artist, 'Lipppa', 'Lipa') AS artist_fixed,
  CASE
    WHEN spotify_streams >= 2000000000 THEN 'Mega hit'
    WHEN spotify_streams >= 1000000000 THEN 'Big streams'
    ELSE 'Growing'
  END AS stream_story
FROM top_songs
WHERE id BETWEEN 1001 AND 1005
ORDER BY track_name;
levels.hintMessage: REPLACE only changes the typo; CASE uses spotify_streams thresholds 2000000000 and 1000000000. Labels: 'Mega hit', 'Big streams', 'Growing'. ORDER BY track_name.
levels.successMessage: That’s the full picture—clean text and readable categories in one SELECT.
